components.gap: Rule sheet and selected derivation definition state different discharge disciplines. The derivation definition (inherited-02193-02340.tex 14-21) lets an application of ->I, neg I, RAA or vee E carry a label i and discharge exactly the open occurrences marked i, i.e. possibly a proper subset of the open occurrences of the bracketed formula, and imposes no freshness requirement on the label an application carries (freshness is stated only for copies, 8-12, and for the merging relabeling, 21-27). The contexted sheet (registry/calculi/nd-cpl.tex 11 and the side conditions at 18, 19, 21, 24) requires the carried label to be fresh from every label of the premise derivations and requires ALL open occurrences of the discharged formula in the witness to be marked and discharged. The sheet therefore admits a strictly narrower set of derivation trees than the definition while claiming (line 11, source comment 5-7) to be the same tree calculus. Policy section 8 requires the sheet to describe that same calculus 'including label freshness and nonempty discharge'. Align the two: either state partial labelled discharge with nonempty marked sets in the sheet, or state total fresh-label discharge in the derivation definition.
